title: Mideast Stocks: Gulf bourses close mixed as shipping security concerns linger

contentHtml:
A trader uses his mobile as he monitors screens displaying stock information at the Saudi Stock Exchange (Tadawul) in Riyadh June 15, 2015. Faisal Al Nasser/ Reuters.

Saudi Arabia's benchmark index eased 0.1%,

Ateeq Shariff | Reuters News

Gulf equities ended mixed on Tuesday as investors weighed the implications of recent tanker attacks and renewed efforts to safeguard key shipping routes. Iran's navy said a fourth oil tanker caught fire within 24 hours after hitting a naval mine in a restricted zone east of the Strait of Hormuz, while Oman's foreign ministry said on Tuesday that Oman and Iran had discussed protecting sea lanes and keeping global trade flowing as Hormuz shipping remains disrupted. 

Saudi Arabia's benchmark index eased 0.1%, hit by a 1.4% fall in oil major Saudi Aramco, as the stock traded ex-dividend. Brent crude futures LCOc1 were up 32 cents, or 0.4%, at $92.76 a barrel by 1204 GMT, as expectations of a supply surplus, driven by recovering Middle East exports, overshadowed concerns about continued attacks on tankers in the region and broader geopolitical tensions. 

Meanwhile, Houthi fighters have taken parts of Yemen's southern coast after Saudi-backed government forces withdrew to protect Aden, military sources said on Monday. Residents are worried the Iran-aligned group will advance on the city. 

Dubai's main share index added 0.6%, helped by a 1.3% gain in blue-chip developer Emaar Properties. In Abu Dhabi, the index advanced 0.9%. Fresh security alerts and new shipping incidents in the region this morning kept investors cautious, even as diplomatic efforts continued. 

Softer oil prices, under pressure from expectations of a supply surplus as Gulf exports recover, added to the wariness around energy-linked stocks, said Daniel Takieddine, Co-founder and CEO of Sky Links Capital Group, The Qatari index lost 0.3%, with the Gulf's biggest lender, Qatar National Bank, retreating 0.6%. 

Outside the Gulf, Egypt's blue-chip index declined 1%, with Talaat Moustafa Group Holding losing 1.8%. 

  • Saudi Arabia fell 0.1% to 10,253 
  • Abu Dhabi gained 0.9% to 9,771 
  • Dubai added 0.6% to 6,248 
  • Qatar eased 0.3% to 10,079
  • Egypt declined 1% to 51,682 
  • Bahrain was up 0.1% to 9,019 
  • Oman lost 0.2% to 7,356 
  • Kuwait inched up 0.1% to 9,019 

(Reporting by Ateeq Shariff in Bengaluru; Editing by Sonia Cheema and Shailesh Kuber)
